newsitem.title: USA: Wall Street seen higher at the open.
newsitem.headline: Wall Street seen higher at the open.

text.p: Wall Street stocks are expected to rise at opening Friday, taking heart from yesterday's gains and bolstered by hopes that a tobacco settlement is imminent, analysts said.
"The market looks firmer based on yesterday's momentum," said Larry Wachtel, an analyst at Prudential Securities.
On Thursday U.S. stocks bounced back after three straight losing sessions, with the Dow Jones Industrial Average rising 58.35 points to 7777.06.
The Nasdaq composite added 14.71 points to 1447.14.

"Yesterday's session was broad-based, which bodes well for today," said Thom Brown, managing director of Rutherford Brown and Catherwood. "The general tone of this market, the strength and breadth of the advance, are really impressive. It's tough to see when it's going to roll over."
In early trade the Standard & Poor's 500 futures index was up three points at 910.50.
Tobacco stocks such as Dow component Philip Morris Cos Inc are likely to rise on hopes that a deal settling hundreds of tobacco-related lawsuits could be announced as early as today, analysts said.
"Talk of an imminent tobacco deal continues to help the tobacco stocks," Brown said.
Negotiations between tobacco industry representatives and state attorneys general have been going on since early April.
The talks are aimed at a broad settlement of legal claims against the industry, in exchange for increased regulation, advertising curbs and health care programs.
Sources involved in the talks said they expected a deal to be announced today.
Japan's Nikkei average closed off 122.31 points at 20,385.54, with investors squaring positions ahead of the weekend and the G7 summit.

In London the FTSE 100 was off 4.3 points at 4649.4. U.S. stocks were firm in London, but trading was thin before the expiration of index futures and options in the United States. Boeing Co added 1/4 to 56-3/4 after British Airways Plc confirmed it had placed a $1 billion order with Boeing.
The long bond was off 5/32 at 6.69 percent.
The dollar extended gains against the yen, trading at 114.60/70 yen in Tokyo.
In Europe the dollar was trading at 1.7276/83 marks.

The Wall Street Journal said in its Heard on the Street column that while oil prices have fallen this year, Exxon Corp's stock price has soared. Analysts say many oil companies have cut costs and become more selective in choosing projects.
The New York Times said in its Market Place column that the strength of the stock market's breadth -- the ratio of advancing issues to declining issues -- may mean prices could go even higher.
